readings: Match each laboratory record to its patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped) and group by patient ID and sex. For each patient, compute the average white blood cell count (`WBC`) and the average of the per-record hemoglobin-to-hematocrit ratio (`HGB` ÷ `HCT` computed for each lab record, then averaged), ignoring missing values. Then take the mean of that ratio across all patients, ignoring missing values, and list the patients whose ratio is greater than that mean. Show patient ID, sex, average WBC, the ratio, and the ratio minus the overall mean. Sort by that difference from largest to smallest (missing values last), return only the first 10 rows, and do not round any values.
queries:
WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.ID,
        p.SEX,
        AVG(l.WBC) AS avg_wbc,
        AVG(l.HGB / l.HCT) AS ratio
    FROM Patient AS p
    JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(ratio) AS mean_ratio
    FROM patient_averages
)
SELECT
    pa.ID,
    pa.SEX,
    pa.avg_wbc,
    pa.ratio,
    pa.ratio - om.mean_ratio AS difference
FROM patient_averages AS pa
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS om
WHERE pa.ratio > om.mean_ratio
ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
